boards.name: Beat sheet
boards.description: Structure a feature screenplay in fifteen beats, placed on a 110-minute timecode ruler so pacing problems are visible at a glance.

cards.title: Beat sheet — “Undertow” (feature, 110 min)
cards.body: Fifteen story beats, each pinned to the minute it should land. Drag a beat on the timeline to see what it does to the pace of the whole film.

cards.title: How to use this template
cards.body: Each card holds what happens at that beat in this story, with the beat’s job in italics underneath. Replace the story, keep the job. Timings are a guide — a page of script is roughly a minute.

cards.title: Running time — beats against the clock
Opening image
cards.body:
Dana sits in her car above the beach she no longer works, engine running, watching the new lifeguards.

*A snapshot of the hero’s world before the story changes it.*

cards.title: Theme stated
cards.body:
Her sister: “You can’t keep everyone out of the water.”

*Someone hints at what the hero must learn.*

cards.title: Set-up
cards.body:
Night shifts at the pool. A town that crosses the street to avoid her. A boy, Sam, who still can’t put his face in the water.

*Home, work, flaws, what is missing.*

cards.title: Catalyst
cards.body:
Sam’s school enters him in the harbour swim. His coach quits. Sam asks for Dana by name.

*The event that knocks life off course.*

cards.title: Debate
cards.body:
She says no twice. His mother says never. Dana watches him fail a length alone.

*Should I go? Can I? The last chance to stay safe.*

cards.title: Break into two
cards.body:
Dawn, the outdoor pool. Dana gets in the water for the first time in four years.

*The hero chooses to act and enters a new world.*

cards.title: B story
cards.body:
Sam’s mother, Leah — the woman who blamed her in court — starts staying to watch.

*A new relationship that carries the theme.*

cards.title: Fun and games
cards.body:
Training montage: breathing drills, cold-water swims, Sam’s first length without stopping.

*The promise of the premise — the trailer moments.*

cards.title: Midpoint
cards.body:
Sam wins the junior heat; the town cheers her for the first time. Leah files a complaint the same night.

*A false victory or false defeat; the stakes rise.*

cards.title: Bad guys close in
cards.body:
Suspended from the pool. Training moves to the sea, in secret, against every rule she taught.

*Pressure from outside and doubt from within.*

cards.title: All is lost
cards.body:
A rip current, a storm, and she freezes — exactly as she did the first time. Sam gets himself out.

*The opposite of the midpoint. Something or someone dies.*

cards.title: Dark night of the soul
cards.body:
At the inquiry transcript, Dana finally reads what really happened four years ago.

*The hero sits in the wreckage — and finally understands.*

cards.title: Break into three
cards.body:
Leah brings Sam to her door: “He won’t swim the harbour without you.”

*Theme and B story give the hero the answer.*

cards.title: Finale
cards.body:
The harbour swim. Dana doesn’t save him — she swims beside him and lets him finish.

*The hero applies what they learned; the old world is remade.*

cards.title: Final image
cards.body:
Dawn on the lifeguard tower, Sam beside her, the car engine off below.

*The opposite of the opening image — proof of change.*

cards.title: Logline
cards.body: A burned-out lifeguard must win back the trust of the town that blamed her for a drowning — by training the boy who survived it.

cards.title: Opening → final image
cards.body:
**Opening:** she sits in her car above the beach she no longer works, engine running.
**Final:** she sits on the lifeguard tower at dawn, the boy beside her, the engine off.

cards.title: Midpoint
cards.body: The boy wins his first open-water race; the town cheers her for the first time in years. False victory: his mother has filed a complaint.

cards.title: All is lost
cards.body: A rip current, a storm, and she freezes — exactly as she did the first time.
